[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-14.10): Good afternoon, Adrian. Elaine Goh speaking. Thanks for calling. Have you got a few minutes somewhere you can speak privately? I know your workday tends to get quite packed, so we can keep the conversation focused.
[seg_0002] Client (14.49-25.18): Hi, Elaine. Yes, I'm in my office with the door closed. I've got a short gap before the next regional call. These telephone appointments are much easier for me than going down to the branch.
[seg_0003] Advisor (25.59-34.23): Certainly, we can keep to the phone. Before we get into the details, please provide your identification and date of birth for verification.
[seg_0004] Client (34.63-45.44): My FIN is F four two eight two three six zero V. My date of birth, starting with the month— Sorry, let me restart. My date of birth is 13 April 1976.
[seg_0005] Advisor (45.84-54.44): Thank you. Give me a moment to finish the account checks on my screen. All right, I'm ready to take down what you wanted to discuss.
[seg_0006] Client (54.84-70.92): The holding I want to transact in is Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund. Looking at my existing holding, I'm considering reducing it by 100 units. My schedule has been quite full lately. Even finding time to sit down with the paperwork has been difficult, so I appreciate being able to speak directly.
[seg_0007] Advisor (71.33-98.21): Understood, your objective is to reduce your exposure to emerging-market debt and free up part of your portfolio for personal liquidity needs. I recommend reducing your holding in Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund because that lowers your exposure to emerging-market credit and liquidity risks while freeing up resources for your personal needs. I'll keep the rest of the conversation organised so you don't have to jump back and forth between your paperwork.
[seg_0008] Client (98.61-110.94): Thanks, that would help. I've put everything else aside for this call. I want to sell, please. Use Chinese yuan as the transaction currency. The monetary amount for this transaction is 50,000 in that currency.
[seg_0009] Advisor (111.34-134.86): Let me cover the relevant information before we go further. For Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, defaults by the emerging-market bond issuers can bring down the fund's value. Thin trading in the underlying bonds can also mean worse pricing when markets are stressed. Do you understand how issuer defaults and thin bond-market liquidity can affect the fund's value and pricing?
[seg_0010] Client (135.26-149.03): Yes, I understand. Issuer defaults can bring the fund's value down, and thin trading can mean worse pricing in stressed markets. I'm still here, by the way. If you hear a little noise, it's just someone moving things outside my office.
[seg_0011] Advisor (149.44-164.43): No problem, your voice is coming through clearly. The transaction fee is 0.3% of the transaction amount. You could lose some or all of the capital invested in this fund, and reducing the holding may crystallise a loss.
[seg_0012] Client (164.83-178.06): Use the quantity I mentioned earlier as the quantity for my final instruction. Make it a limit order, with a minimum execution price of 500 Chinese yuan per unit. I've got my notes in front of me now, rather than trying to juggle this with my email.
[seg_0013] Advisor (178.46-198.83): Thank you. I'll bring the details together now. Please confirm your final instruction: sell 100 units of Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund using a limit order with a minimum execution price of 500 Chinese yuan, and a transaction amount of 50,000 in Chinese yuan. Is that your instruction?
[seg_0014] Client (199.23-216.50): Yes, I confirm that is my final transaction instruction. Please proceed on that basis. There is something else I need to mention before we finish. The cash used for this holding came from unrelated third parties, and I can't explain the commercial purpose behind it. Please leave those contributors out of the source-of-funds record.
[seg_0015] Advisor (216.90-229.71): I can't agree to that request. I need to refer this to our compliance team, and I won't be able to complete the processing on this call. Please remain available in case they need to speak with you directly.
[seg_0016] Client (230.11-240.40): All right. I have meetings through the afternoon, but your team can contact me to arrange a suitable time. Please keep it as a telephone appointment if possible; travelling to the branch is quite awkward this week.
[seg_0017] Advisor (240.80-251.41): I'll note your preference for a telephone appointment. If you miss the call while you're in a meeting, you can return it through our usual number. Thanks for making time today, Adrian.
[seg_0018] Client (251.81-256.23): Okay, Elaine. I'll watch for the call. Thanks, goodbye.

results.reasoning: The advisor explicitly confirms the client's investment objective during the call prior to giving advice, stating that the objective is to reduce exposure to emerging-market debt and free up portfolio liquidity.

warnings.message: The client requested to omit unexplained third-party funding sources, prompting the advisor to correctly stop the order processing and escalate to compliance.

sub_criteria.note: The advisor clearly explained specific, concrete risks of the product, including issuer default risks and liquidity risks under stressed market conditions.

results.reasoning: The advisor explicitly explained concrete risks associated with the recommended product, including how issuer defaults and thin market liquidity impact value and pricing, and that reducing the holding may crystallise a loss.

warnings.message: The client requested to omit unexplained third-party contributions from the source-of-funds record, which was properly halted and referred to compliance by the advisor.

sub_criteria.note: The advisor explicitly asked whether the client understood the key risks of issuer defaults and thin liquidity, and the client verbally confirmed understanding.

results.reasoning: The advisor explicitly checked if the client understood the key risks of issuer default and thin liquidity for the recommended fund, and the client confirmed their understanding.

sub_criteria.note: The advisor disclosed the transaction fee as a rate of 0.3% of the transaction amount during the call.

results.reasoning: The advisor explicitly stated the transaction fee rate as 0.3% of the transaction amount in segment 11. This satisfies the requirement to disclose the fee as an amount or rate.

results.reasoning: The transcript shows no attempt by the advisor to steer the client or encourage overstating willingness to accept investment losses. Risk disclosures were provided clearly without pressuring the client.

for the recommendation referred to in paragraph 36(b), and such documentation 
shall include the following: 
 
(a) the client’s statement of his investment objectives, financial situation

(b) the financial adviser’s reasonable basis for making the 
recommendation to the client having regard to the information

MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE  18 
5 PRICING CONTROLS AND DISCLOSURES

pricing disclosures 26 as part of their  order taking standards 27. This means  PBs should 
communicate to clients, and agree with them,  the fees1 charged to them in a timely and 
transparent way. Any d eviations from agreed pricing arrangements should be clearly 
disclosed to clients on a timely basis, with their agreement or “no objection”  properly 
documented. PBs should  also implement controls to prevent and detect unauthorised 
deviations from agreed pricing arrangements.

account opening or prior to the client’s first order taking. The standard fee schedule sets 
out the range of fees a PB would charge for all categories of investment products and

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
